text:
cheng: CI microbench alert on PR 9799 — batcher_latency_micro increased +12% vs golden (threshold +5%). CI link: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/9799/microbench
maria: seeing the same locally on my rtx-microperf run. tail latency up, p95 shifted ~40ms. attaching perf counters.
ryan: ugh. any obvious diffs in the kernel selector changes on that PR? last merged change touched autoselect heuristics right?
cheng: yes PR 9788 merged earlier today. commit abcdef1234 "autoselect: bias kernel cost towards throughput on long seqs". suspect cost-model tweak.
ci-bot: [CI] microbench job failed: https://ci.redwood/build/9799/microbench — threshold_diff:+12.02%
perf-bot: Recorded perf snapshot: kv_hit_rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.63 for workloads with seq<128 after the change.
maria: raw logs excerpt:
```
[kv-cache] hit_rate=0.872
[kv-cache] hit_rate=0.632  <-- after merge
[batcher] avg_wait_ms=6.4 -> 9.1
[kernel] selected=matmul_fast_quant (switched from matmul_cache_friendly)
```
cheng: interesting — kernel change could increase memory pressure on KV cache / warmup behavior. The autoselect change nudged selector to pick lower-cost-per-token kernels that increase working set, evicting KV entries.
ryan: can we bisect quickly? steps I'd run:
```
git checkout origin/main
git bisect start --term-old="golden" --term-new="failing"
git bisect good <commit-before-9788>
git bisect bad abcdef1234
# run microbench script
```
maria: I ran a short bisect toy and it pointed to abcdef1234 -> same commit. Repro is stable under the microbench harness.
cheng: proof snippet from local run (reduced):
```
commit abcdef1234
kv_hit=0.63 p95=132ms baseline_kv_hit=0.87 p95=98ms
```
ryan: propose two-step response: 1) quick revert patch to restore previous cost bias (open PR), 2) add unit test that asserts kv_hit_rate delta < 0.05 on our canonical seq<128 smoke harness.
maria: +1 on revert. I'll draft the microbench guard test and add it to perf CI. Also add a telemetry assertion to console which emits kvcache delta when rolling out.
cheng: I'll prepare a revert PR and include a regression note — also propose follow-up to refactor kernel selector to expose working-set estimate so we don't regress KV hit silently.
ci-bot: revert PR created: https://ci.redwood/pr/9800 — running perf validation
perf-bot: note: this change also affected model-quantized path selection; add a quick checklist to validate quant kernels vs kvcache in the lab.
ryan: assigning @maria to perf test, @cheng to revert PR, I'll review immediately. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:
maria: will post perf diffs once CI on 9800 finishes. thanks all.
